subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 28-year-old woman has excessive worry about work, school, and her children on most days for the past 8 months. She has difficulty concentrating, is restless, is irritable, and reports muscle tension and poor sleep.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: GAD is excessive anxiety and worry about different aspects of daily life for most days of at least 6 months, associated with at least 3 of CRIMES symptoms (difficulty Concentrating, Restlessness, Irritability, Muscle tension, low Energy, Sleep disturbance; at least 1 in children). This patient has worry for 8 months plus concentration difficulty, restlessness, irritability, muscle tension, and sleep disturbance.

explanation_incorrect.A: Panic disorder requires recurrent panic attacks with at least 1 month of aftermath; discrete attacks are not described.
explanation_incorrect.C: Social anxiety disorder is fear of embarrassment in social situations, not broad daily-life worry.
explanation_incorrect.D: Agoraphobia is avoidance of at least 2 situations due to fear that help or escape is unavailable, not generalized worry.
explanation_incorrect.E: Adjustment disorder is symptoms within 3 months of an identifiable stressor, not 8 months of pervasive worry.

educationalObjective: GAD is excessive worry most days for at least 6 months with at least 3 CRIMES symptoms (concentration, restlessness, irritability, muscle tension, energy, sleep).

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 42-year-old man with GAD has not responded to an adequate trial of an SSRI and CBT. His psychiatrist is considering second-line options.
question: Which of the following is considered second-line treatment for GAD?
explanation_correct: For GAD, CBT, SSRIs, and SNRIs such as venlafaxine are first-line. Second-line options include buspirone, TCAs, and benzodiazepines. After failing first-line SSRI and CBT, buspirone is an appropriate next step. Benzodiazepines are also second-line but are useful for acute relief.

explanation_incorrect.A: CBT is a first-line treatment for GAD, not second-line.
explanation_incorrect.B: Venlafaxine is an SNRI and is considered first-line for GAD, not second-line.
explanation_incorrect.D: SSRIs are first-line for GAD; he has already failed one.
explanation_incorrect.E: Psychoeducation and exercise are helpful adjuncts but are not the designated second-line pharmacologic step after failing first-line therapy.

educationalObjective: GAD is treated first line with CBT, SSRIs, and SNRIs; buspirone, TCAs, and benzodiazepines are second-line.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 25-year-old woman worries excessively about several aspects of daily life. Her symptoms have been present for only 3 months, and she has two associated CRIMES symptoms.
question: Which of the following best explains why she does not yet meet DSM-5 criteria for GAD?

options.text: GAD requires excessive worry most days for at least 6 months and at least 3 CRIMES symptoms in adults
GAD requires the presence of panic attacks
GAD requires symptoms for at least 1 month

explanation_correct: GAD requires excessive anxiety and worry about different aspects of daily life for most days of at least 6 months, plus at least 3 CRIMES symptoms in adults (at least 1 in children). This patient has only 3 months of symptoms and two associated symptoms, so she does not meet criteria. Panic attacks and psychotic features are not required.

explanation_incorrect.B: Panic attacks are not required for GAD; they are characteristic of panic disorder.
explanation_incorrect.C: GAD affects adults as well as children; adults require at least 3 CRIMES symptoms.
explanation_incorrect.D: Psychotic features are not part of GAD and would suggest a psychotic disorder.
explanation_incorrect.E: GAD requires at least 6 months, not merely 1 month of symptoms.

educationalObjective: GAD requires excessive worry most days for at least 6 months plus at least 3 CRIMES symptoms in adults; shorter duration or fewer symptoms does not meet criteria.
